text: Operations report failure by returning a {ok:false, reason} result with fixed reason strings instead of throwing.
Withdrawals are capped by a daily limit of 5000.00 per account.
The daily withdrawal counter never resets, so the 'daily' limit is effectively a lifetime limit.
Only the withdrawal amount, not the fee, counts toward the daily limit.
The insufficient-funds check runs before the daily-limit check, deciding which rejection reason wins.
The withdrawal fee is capped at a maximum of 25.00.
The 1% fee is rounded up to the next cent (ceil, with a 1e-9 epsilon) rather than to nearest.
A withdrawal is rejected unless the balance covers amount plus fee; no overdraft is allowed.
The withdrawal and its fee are debited and recorded as one combined 'withdrawal' entry instead of a separate fee entry.
Transfers and splits are rejected if the sender's balance would go negative.
Transfers and split payments charge no fee.
Cent rounding adds a 1e-7 epsilon before Math.round to counter floating-point error.
Foreign deposits are rounded with the half-away-from-zero helper rather than half-to-even.
The exchange rate must be positive, and a bad rate is reported as 'invalid-amount'.
A foreign deposit that converts to zero cents is rejected as 'amount-too-small'.
A positive amount that rounds to zero cents (e.g. 0.001) is accepted for deposit, withdrawal, transfer and split, recording a 0.00 entry (a withdrawal is still charged the minimum fee).
Infinity passes the positive-amount check and is accepted as an amount.
A repeated transaction id returns success without checking that the retry carries the same account, amount or operation type.
Transaction ids are deduplicated in one global namespace across all accounts and operation types.
Input validation runs before the duplicate check, so a retry with invalid input is rejected rather than treated as a replay.
Rejected operations do not record their transaction id, so the same id can later succeed.
Unknown accounts are created implicitly by any operation, including as withdrawal or transfer source and even when the operation is then rejected.
Querying an unknown account returns balance 0 and empty history instead of an error.
Account ids and transaction ids are not validated; empty strings are accepted.
A transfer to the same account is accepted, writing a transfer-out and a transfer-in entry on that account.
Split remainder cents go one each to the first recipients in list order.
A split with an empty recipient list is rejected as 'no-recipients'.
Split allows duplicate recipients and the sender among the recipients.
Interest takes the annual rate as a percentage, not a fraction.
Interest is simple (not compounded) over the given days.
Interest is rounded down to the cent (floor with a 1e-7 epsilon).
Interest rate and days must be positive; fractional days are accepted.
Interest that rounds to zero returns success but records no entry and does not mark the transaction id as seen.
History entries store amounts as positive decimal units, with direction implied only by kind.
balance() and entry amounts are returned as floating-point currency units (cents/100), not cents.
